svg.text: • Generation mix: wind, solar, hydro, CC
• Gas supply, EU ETS carbon & geopolitics
• Local Ollama inference (zero internet / no data leakage)
Features conditioned only on data published up to t−1.
Forward-filling weekend quotes with NO_TRADE masks.
Z-score scalers fit strictly on historical training slice D_train.
Confirms sentiment signals add orthogonal variance to grid.
▸ NLP vs Quant: Full vs Quant +1.59 pp (2025)
▸ NLP vs Base: Hybrid vs Common +4.18 pp (2025)
▸ Text vs Commodities: Hybrid better during 2026 shock
▸ Noise robustness: Curated vs uncurated news
Action space A: 14 discrete contracts (SPOT, D1–D3, W1–W4, M1–M6)
Observation oₜ: 7-day lagged state + 400-day forward inventory queue cₜ
Clearing rules: OMIClear variation margins + OMIE physical delivery
Rolling update horizons W ∈ {1, 3, 6, 12} months across 2023–2026
Bounded compute budget (K = 15,000 steps/month; warm-start updates)
1. Core Empirical Findings & Downside Risk Protection
Mitigated maximum drawdown: reduced by ~66% vs D3 (186.45 vs 548.95 €/MWh).
Lower downside risk: σ₋ = 9.15 €/MWh (vs 13.68 for D2 and 18.63 for D3).
Dynamic multi-horizon allocation: hedging across D2, D1, SPOT, and D3.
Attribution shows the policy uses news sentiment.
Leading signals: regulatory risk (φ₆), LNG (φ₄), generation mix (φ₇).
Policy avoids overpriced long-dated contracts in falling markets.
Savings persist with fees up to 0.25 €/MWh across 5 seeds.
